summaryPoints: Australia recovered from early pressure in the first innings, anchored by Steve Smith's resolute 178 to post 451.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at JSCA International Stadium Complex commenced with high tactical intensity as Australia posted 451/10 (137.3 ov) in their opening innings. In response, India countered with 603/9 (209.6 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 6-Wicket Spell: Ravindra Jadeja (6/124), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Ravindra Jadeja delivered a masterclass for India (54 Runs & 10 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Match Drawn 47%) and allowing Match Drawn to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Australia faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Match Drawn's bowling unit, bolstered by Cheteshwar Pujara (202 Runs), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Match drawn in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Match Drawn's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Australia produced fighting phases, Match Drawn won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
